_comment: The packaged library is written in English by repository policy, but the
people searching it work in Chinese. The corpus holds only a few hundred
distinct Chinese characters, almost all incidental, so a Chinese query
scores on whichever characters happen to appear rather than on its subject.
Every concept below already exists in the corpus under its English name;
what is missing is the route from one to the other.
Direction is one-way: a query term expands to corpus terms, never the
reverse. Expanding a narrow term into a broad one (Ascend -> every NPU)
would widen results rather than find them, so entries stay specific.
Values are spellings verified to occur in this corpus. A term whose English
form is absent does not belong here; it belongs in the corpus first.
Keep the list short: a broad alias costs precision on every query that
touches it, and an unused one is upkeep with no return. Add a term when a
real query misses because of it.
JSON rather than YAML because the base install is PyYAML-free by contract.
synonyms: English terms the corpus and its readers spell differently. Same one-way, query-side rule as aliases; listed separately so the Chinese map stays a translation table rather than a thesaurus.
